extracted.intended_audience: designers, vendors, internal staff, and corporate partners producing branded materials for United Way of Greater Knoxville
extracted.subtask_description: Brand guidance for using United Way of Greater Knoxville visual identity: logo, clear space, prohibited treatments, typography, color palette, and accessibility for printed and digital communications. Intended to ensure consistent, legible, and on-brand creative across partners and materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full-Color Logo (Preferred)
rubrics_metrics.description: The full-color version of the logo is preferred and, whenever possible, should be used on all branded materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not adjust the colors of the logo symbol in any way. The United Way logotype is blue unless there is low contrast with the background, in which case it should contrast for clarity and legibility when used with photography.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knockout (White) Logo Usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The knockout (white) version is for use on dark backgrounds or photographs where the full-color logo will not work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using this version, ensure that the background is dark for clarity and legibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-Color (Black) Logo Usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The one-color (black) version is for use in applications where full-color or knockout logos would not be appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for grayscale or one-color printing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logo Color Integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: The logo symbol colors must not be altered under any circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain original logo colors; do not recolor or modify the symbol or logotype. (Reinforces 'Do not change the logo’s colors' in the Logo Don'ts.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Logo Clear Space
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a minimum amount of clear space around the logo to keep it clear of competing text, images, and graphics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum clear space is equal to the height of the letter 'U' of the logo on all sides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logo Don'ts (Prohibited Treatments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific prohibited alterations and treatments of the logo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rotate the logo; do not change the logo’s colors; do not crop the logo; do not skew, distort, or stretch the logo; do not add a drop shadow; do not add artistic effects; do not use translucency; do not integrate the logo into messaging (i.e., replace an “O” with the logo). The document states: 'it should not be altered under any circumstances.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Typography Hierarchy and Usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on headline, sub-headline, body copy, and pull-quote typefaces and hierarchy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Headlines: ANTONIO BOLD (all-uppercase style suitable for bold headlines and large-scale messaging). Sub-headlines: Palanquin SemiBold. Body copy: Palanquin Regular. Pull quotes: Palanquin Bold. Palanquin Medium used for certain body text. Use typography and color to establish a consistent messaging hierarchy and create clear, compelling messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Italics
rubrics_metrics.description: Italics are not recommended for brand typography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document: 'We do not recommend the use of italics. The italics appear disruptive with our headline font (or the alternate brand font Noto).'

rubrics_metrics.name: All-Caps and Multiple-Line Headline Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: All-uppercase style is suitable for bold headlines and large-scale messaging; a 'Multiple Line Headlines Rule' is noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ANTONIO in all-uppercase for bold, large headlines and adhere to the Multiple Line Headlines Rule (i.e., apply the all-caps/headline treatment only under the specified multi-line headline conditions shown in examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate and Special-Use Fonts
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternate fonts and special use fonts for specific contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Noto as an alternate brand font (available at fonts.google.com). A special-use font is available for occasions requiring a more sophisticated style (e.g., fundraising). Fonts availability and fallbacks (Arial family, various Palanquin weights, Noto Serif/Sans variants) are listed and should be used as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary Color Palette
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary colors are derived from the logo symbol and are blue, red, and yellow; each has four shades to provide dimension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preferred shade (used in the logo) should be used prominently; these primary colors should be applied across communications unless in a black-and-white context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary and Tertiary Colors
rubrics_metrics.description: Secondary color is green; tertiary colors are purple and black.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use secondary and tertiary colors in supporting roles in communications, not as the main or dominant color. They may be used as accents to add visual interest but should not take precedence over primary colors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color Usage Hierarchy and Application
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for combining and applying primary, secondary, tertiary colors and tones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core communications should prominently feature at least one, but preferably all three, primary colors as the dominant color(s). Primary color tones can add texture and depth but should not replace the primary colors. Secondary and tertiary colors may be applied alongside primaries to add contrast and clarity; see 'Bringing the Elements to Life' examples for application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color Accessibility and Contrast
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure communications are accessible by using approved color combinations that meet accessibility standards and contrast ratios.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When choosing typography and background colors, always promote visibility and legibility by ensuring adequate contrast. The guideline lists acceptable combinations (examples include: blue text on white background; red text on white background; dark blue text on white; white text on blue or red backgrounds; black text on yellow background; dark blue text on yellow; and several large/bold text combinations). Refer to the contrast ratio guidelines in the document for exact thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency and Cohesion in Application
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain consistency and cohesion across all brand communications when applying typography and color.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the brand elements (logo, color, type) consistently across materials to ensure recognizable and cohesive communications. Refer to later example pages (Bringing the Elements to Life) for concrete applications and examples.
